titleStmt.title: Telegram From the Embassy in Ecuador to the Department of State

div.head: 371. Telegram From the Embassy in Ecuador to the Department of State
div.p: 5289. Subject: Letter from President Reagan to President Hurtado.

2. I delivered the signed original of the President’s letter (reftel) to President Hurtado on July 21. Hurtado, who had already seen the message which was transmitted through the Foreign Ministry upon receipt of the cabled text, expressed his personal satisfaction at receiving the original letter. He made two substantive comments regarding the President’s letter:

list.label: A.
list.item: Hurtado stated he was determined to reciprocate President Reagan’s hope to eliminate obstacles hindering improved bilateral relations and he affirmed his intention to maintain the best possible relationships with the U.S. He commented that as Vice President he had followed our cooperation in development closely and that he would continue to do so from the presidency. These remarks offered me the opening to bring up our technical talks with the Foreign Ministry on fisheries, which I said constituted a good example of how both governments could work together to overcome bilateral problems. Hurtado said he was pleased at these efforts to find practical solutions to our tuna problems without prejudice to our juridical positions on LOS and repeated his determination to maintain good relations with the U.S.
list.label: B.
list.item:
President Hurtado also referred to President Reagan’s remarks regarding joint endeavors to encourage the development of more humane and secure societies elsewhere. He said he was very concerned about the situation in Central America; not only El Salvador but also Guatemala. Hurtado said we should talk about what can be done to alleviate suffering and violence in Central America while assuring the right of self-determination in those countries. I said the USG shares his concerns and referred to the Nassau conference in which the Governments of Canada, Mexico, Venezuela and the U.S. consulted on a Caribbean Basin development initiative. We agreed that Central America and Caribbean Basin should be a topic for discussion when Ambassador Kirkpatrick calls on him on her forthcoming
visit to Quito.

div.p: 3. After our meeting, I sent the President the Spanish text of Ambassador Enders’ speech on El Salvador with a note referring to our conversation.

note.p: Source: Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D810344–1030. Confidential; Priority. Sent for information to Guayaquil and USUN.

In telegram 174484 to Quito, July 2, the Department sent the text of a letter from Reagan for delivery to Hurtado. In the letter, Reagan shared condolences regarding the death President Roldós and hope that Ecuador and Peru “resume direct, high-level conversations and dispel the present atmosphere of mutual distrust,” as well as for improved bilateral relations with “hemispheric cooperation.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D810311–0403) The signed original of Reagan’s letter has not been found. Copies of both the Spanish language original and a translation of Hurtado’s August 12 letter of reply are in the Reagan Library, Roger W. Fontaine Files, Subject File, Ecuador [July 1981–December 1981].

In telegram 5823 from Quito, August 13, the Embassy sent a report on Kirkpatrick’s August 11 meetings with Hurtado and Barrera. Kirkpatrick told Hurtado that the “only purpose of her trip was to begin what US hoped would be frequent consultations between the two governments.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D810379–0368)
See Department of State Bulletin, September 1981, pp. 70–73.
